item.subject: science
item.stem: In a government school in Pune, a measles vaccination camp is held before the monsoon. Meera's grandmother asks why healthy children are being vaccinated. Which statement best explains how vaccination reduces serious infections and their spread?

options.A: Vaccines are medicines taken after someone falls sick, so they cure measles and stop it spreading.
options.B: Vaccines prepare the immune system before exposure, so vaccinated children are less likely to become seriously ill and less likely to pass the infection to others.
options.C: The first exposure to measles produces the stronger immune response, so vaccination is only useful after a child has already had measles once.
options.D: Children in the same class share the same immunity, so vaccinating a few children protects the whole class equally.
